fields.reasoning: The brief allows a virtual or a scaled clock. Scripts poll for work other processes do (fake agents, background rhiza commands), which needs some real time to happen; a clock whose Sleep returns at once turns each such poll into a busy loop on a shared 4-core VM that has already been OOM-crashed once, while a scaled clock with a floor keeps every poll a real, cheap wait.
fields.statement: Testscripts get a scaled clock, not one where Sleep returns at once: each Sleep(d) waits d divided by a scale in real time (at least 1 ms) while Now advances by the whole d, so waits, polls, backoffs and timeouts keep their order and count but cost about a thousandth of their wall time; production keeps RealClock

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/run -run TestScaledClock shows: at scale 1000 Sleep(30*time.Second) returns within 100 ms of real time and Now has advanced at least 30 s; Sleep(time.Microsecond) still waits at least 1 ms; with RHIZA_TEST_CLOCK_SCALE unset or empty the chosen clock is RealClock; failure cases: values 0, -5, 1.5 and abc each give RealClock and no panic. Touches internal/run/engine.go or a new internal/run/clock.go and its _test.go. Must not change RealClock, the Engine's nil-Clock default or any workflow's poll or backoff value.
fields.statement: internal/run has a scaled Clock, chosen by RHIZA_TEST_CLOCK_SCALE=<n>, whose Sleep(d) waits d/n of real time (never less than 1 ms) and whose Now runs n times faster than the wall clock from its start; with the variable unset, empty or not a positive integer the engine keeps RealClock.

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath -v ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/(run-ship-conflict-fix|run-ship-ci-fix|run-ship-main-dispatch-fail|arbiter-agent-tabs|plan-workflow-ci-infra-wait)$' passes with each script's elapsed under 30 s (2026-11-15: 195, 173, 130, 108 and 96 s); go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run 'TestRunClock' shows runClock is RealClock with the variable unset and the scaled clock with it set; failure case: a script that clears it (env RHIZA_TEST_CLOCK_SCALE=) runs on RealClock, shown by a short wait-timeout script in cmd/rhiza/testdata/script. Speedup measure (orchestrator, quiet VM): go clean -testcache && /usr/bin/time -f '%e s' go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza, against 639 s. Touches internal/api/run.go, run_spawn.go, api.go, ship.go, session.go, ship_deploy.go, their tests, and cmd/rhiza/main_test.go. Must not change a production interval, a workflow .toml, or the daemon, feed and session-limit tickers.
fields.statement: When RHIZA_TEST_CLOCK_SCALE is set, every wait a run makes goes by the scaled clock: internal/api's runClock (run.start and run.resume polls, wait conditions and backoff), the spawn poll in run_spawn.go, the default ctx.Sleep in api.go, ship.go and session.go, and ship_deploy.go's interval; cmd/rhiza/main_test.go's Setup sets it to 1000 for every script, so the builtin workflows' 30 s polls and 2 min backoff cost milliseconds in scripts.
